personalInfo.storyContent:
I am **Lê Trí Trung** (born 2005) — Founder & Head of Technology (Tech Lead / Software Architect) at **SynapForge Venture Studio** in Da Nang, specializing in architecting and operating high-performance digital platforms, SaaS Automation, and AI Engineering for businesses.

My technical foundation is grounded in strong academics at **[FPT University Da Nang](/achievements?tab=education)** (Software Engineering major, **GPA 3.3/4.0 - 8.2/10.0**), having been selected as an **[International Student Exchange Representative](/achievements?tab=education)** in **Technology Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia** (12/2023), certified with **IELTS 6.0** (IDP Education issued 04/2026), and graduated from **Phan Chau Trinh Gifted High School** with a **GPA of 9.0/10.0**.

In terms of technological honors, I was awarded **[Winner (First Place) of the Hackathon Computer Vision 2026](/achievements?tab=prizes)** (FPT Education), reached the **[National Finals of InnoCodeCamp 2025](/achievements?tab=prizes)** as Team Leader, the **[National Finals of ResFres 2024](/achievements?tab=prizes)**, and co-authored an **[International Scientific Research Paper (ICTA 2026)](/achievements?tab=prizes)** on AI Fine-tuning for automated detection and remediation of race-condition vulnerabilities in codebases.

In real-world product delivery, I have led 3 core venture pillars:
1. **[Biensovip.com](/projects/26) (Solo Software Architect):** Architected and coded end-to-end an exclusive license plate marketplace and valuation platform from scratch on .NET 8 / ASP.NET Core (Clean Architecture), 61 PostgreSQL entity tables optimized with GIN indexing (<8ms queries), VietQR Webhook auto-settlement (<0.5s), DeepSeek AI Chatbot, and Linux VPS orchestration.
2. **[The MC Hub](/projects/11) (CEO & Tech Lead):** Led a 6-engineer team launching an AI voice training platform (React 19 + Spring Boot 3.3 + Python FastAPI & Whisper), successfully monetizing in month one with 87 professional MCs and 20 subscription transactions.
3. **[BrandHub](/projects/14) (Tech Lead & Solutions Architect):** Architected a 7-microservice multi-channel brand management ecosystem (Spring Cloud Gateway, RabbitMQ DLQ exponential retry, Java 21, Python GraphRAG).

Beyond software, I have served as a **professional MC hosting 50+ major events (600–1,000+ attendees)**, served as Head Referee for FPTU AI & Robotics 2025, and am the **[Founder of The Dreamers Charity Organization](/activities)** (30+ members) spreading technology education to underprivileged children.

projectItems.description:
A full-stack **job search platform** built with a cross-functional Agile team of 6. I owned the **backend architecture** — designing and building RESTful APIs with **Java Spring Boot**, managing relational data in **SQL Server**, and wiring in an **AI-powered chatbot** to help job seekers with resume tips and job matching.

My main contributions were the **authentication system** (JWT-based login/register), the **job posting and application flow APIs**, and setting up a **Git branching strategy** (feature branches + pull requests) that kept the whole team's work clean across 4 months of development.

The platform is live on Vercel and still evolving, with real-time job alerts and an employer dashboard in the pipeline.
projectItems.challenge: We needed a job platform where seekers could search and apply while getting AI help (resume tips, job matching), all while a 6-person team stayed coordinated on one codebase for 4 months without stepping on each other's toes.
highlights: Designed and built the full RESTful API in Java Spring Boot, managing relational data in SQL Server
Built a JWT-based authentication system (login/register) from scratch
Set up a Git branching strategy (feature branch + pull request) that kept a 6-person team's work clean across 4 months
Integrated an AI chatbot to help job seekers with resume tips and job matching

projectItems.description:
Led a **4-member team** in building a full e-commerce platform for a bakery — covering the product catalog, order management, shopping cart, and customer accounts. I architected the **Java Servlets backend**, designed the **SQL Server database schema**, and split up work across the team using weekly sprints.

Standout pieces included an **AI-powered chatbot** for customer support (wired in via API), **Google Maps API** for store locations, and **Google OAuth** for social login. The frontend was plain **HTML/CSS/JavaScript**, which kept the whole thing light and fast.

This was my first real team project, and it taught me a lot — how to scope features realistically, how to work through merge conflicts when the deadline's looming, and how to actually ship a finished product end-to-end.
projectItems.challenge: My first team project — I needed to help build a complete e-commerce platform (catalog, cart, orders, customer accounts) for a bakery, with a 4-person team, a fixed deadline, and zero prior experience coordinating a team.
highlights: Architected the backend in Java Servlets and designed the SQL Server database schema from scratch
Led a 4-person team, splitting tasks into weekly sprints
Integrated an AI chatbot for customer support, Google Maps API for store location, and Google OAuth for social login
Learned to resolve merge conflicts under deadline pressure and ship a complete product end-to-end

projectItems.description:
I founded and lead **The Dreamers** — a student-run charity at FPT University focused on making a real difference through technology and education. The organization runs hands-on programs bringing **coding workshops, communication skills training, and mentorship** directly to orphaned children and underprivileged youth.

As founder, I handle the full operational picture: recruiting and onboarding members, setting the project roadmap, coordinating with partner organizations, and running fundraising campaigns that have funded multiple charity missions.

Events we've organized include **Tốt Hy Vọng**, **Vòng vào Mộng mơ**, **Dream High**, and a **Charity Music Performance** — each one requiring full planning, logistics, and team coordination from start to finish. We're also building a backend platform in **Java Spring Boot** to manage member activity and event records.
projectItems.challenge: Building a student charity that actually lasts — not just running one-off events, but keeping the whole thing running: recruiting members, fundraising, and now digitizing member and activity management with a dedicated backend platform.
highlights: Founded and run the entire operation: member recruitment, project roadmap, and fundraising across multiple charity campaigns
Organized 4 major events end-to-end: Tot Hy Vong, Vong vao Mong mo, Dream High, Charity Music Performance
Currently building a backend to manage activities and member records in Java Spring Boot

projectItems.description:
A focused utility built in 10 days to automate repetitive web form submissions — cutting out manual data entry for structured, high-volume input work.

The backend uses **Node.js** to drive form interaction through DOM scripting, paired with a lightweight **React frontend** that lets users upload data (CSV/JSON), preview it, and fire off batch submissions with one click. I built it to handle the annoying edge cases too — validation delays, fields that render dynamically, and CAPTCHA-protected forms.

This one sharpened my sense of how the browser DOM actually behaves, how async scripting patterns hold up in practice, and where automation hits its real limits — useful groundwork for QA, data tooling, and internal workflow automation.
projectItems.challenge: Cut out repetitive manual data entry for high-volume web forms, on a tight 10-day deadline — and handle tricky cases like dynamic field rendering and CAPTCHA-protected forms along the way.
highlights: Built a Node.js DOM-control engine to automate form interaction
React frontend for uploading CSV/JSON, previewing entries, and batch-submitting with one click
Handled edge cases: validation delays, dynamic field rendering, CAPTCHA-protected forms
Shipped solo, start to finish, in 10 days

projectItems.description:
A complete e-commerce bookstore built entirely on the **OutSystems low-code platform** — part of my internship training at **FPT Software**, where OutSystems gets used in real enterprise client work.

The app covers the core e-commerce flows: **product catalog with search/filter**, **shopping cart**, **order management**, and a basic **admin panel** for inventory. Building it fully in OutSystems taught me how to think about data models, UI logic, and API integrations inside a visual dev environment — skills that translate directly to enterprise rapid-delivery work.

The live demo is publicly available on OutSystems Cloud.
projectItems.challenge: Learn and ship a full e-commerce app entirely inside a visual development environment (OutSystems) — a skillset that applies directly to enterprise rapid-delivery projects at FPT Software.
highlights: Built the full e-commerce flow: catalog with search/filter, cart, order management, admin panel for inventory
Learned to reason about data models, UI logic, and API integrations in a low-code environment
Live demo publicly accessible on OutSystems Cloud

projectItems.description:
A pixel-accurate clone of the TikTok web interface, built as a structured practice project through the **F8 React course** — one of Vietnam's most respected frontend learning programs.

The goal was to really nail **React component architecture**: breaking the TikTok UI into reusable, composable pieces — Sidebar, VideoFeed, UserCard, ActionBar — each one handling its own props, state, and effects properly. Along the way I practiced **custom hooks**, **React Router** for multi-page navigation, **CSS Modules** for scoped styling, and building a fully responsive layout with no UI library.

This project locked in my React fundamentals before I carried them into production work like Job Finder and The MC Hub.
projectItems.challenge: Solidify my React fundamentals before carrying them into production projects (Job Finder, The MC Hub) — by precisely rebuilding a complex, highly interactive real-world UI (TikTok web).
highlights: Split the UI into reusable components — Sidebar, VideoFeed, UserCard, ActionBar — with properly managed props/state/effects
Practiced custom hooks, React Router for multi-page navigation, CSS Modules for scoped styling
Built a fully responsive layout with zero UI library

projectItems.description:
This portfolio — the site you're on right now. Designed and built from scratch, with the focus on **clean aesthetics, performance, and real content** rather than a template.

The design follows a **monochrome + pastel color system** inspired by modern Figma trends: oversized type, pill-shaped buttons, pastel accent blocks, and consistent spacing throughout. Every page gets a custom **PageBanner**, animated entries via **Framer Motion**, and layouts that hold up fully responsive down to mobile.

Under the hood it's a **React 19 (CRA)** app using **React Router v6** for navigation, inline styles for component-scoped design, and CSS media queries for responsive breakpoints. Content flows from a central `data.js` file, so updates are simple without touching component logic.
projectItems.challenge: Build a portfolio that actually feels like quality work — avoiding that templated look, keeping performance tight (code-splitting, lazy images), and making content easy to update through a central data layer instead of editing components directly.
highlights: Designed a custom monochrome + pastel block color system instead of grabbing an off-the-shelf theme
Data-driven architecture: all content flows from data.js, decoupled from component logic
Route-level code-splitting, image optimization via Cloudinary, bilingual EN/VI i18n
Consistent Framer Motion animation across the site, respecting prefers-reduced-motion

projectItems.description:
A full-stack internal management system for bakery operations — built as a course assignment, but scoped like a real product. Covers **inventory tracking**, **sales recording**, **order management**, and a **customer database**, all wired together through a REST API layer.

The backend is **Java Spring Boot** with **MySQL** for persistence, feeding a **React** frontend deployed on Vercel. I handled both sides myself: API design, database schema, React component structure, and the deployment pipeline.

Building this solo really cemented my understanding of the full request lifecycle — from a click in the UI down to a database query and back — and gave me the confidence to design a system end-to-end without teammates to lean on.
projectItems.challenge: A course assignment with real-world scope (inventory, sales, orders, customer database), but done solo — meaning I had to design and ship the entire system myself, from database to deployment, with no one to split the work with.
highlights: Designed the API and database schema entirely solo
Java Spring Boot + MySQL backend, React frontend deployed on Vercel
Owned the full pipeline solo: API design → database → component structure → deployment

projectItems.description:
A **Vietnamese agricultural marketplace** connecting farmers, suppliers, and customers — covering listings, orders, reviews, and notifications. It started as an academic project (**PRM393**) with a **Flutter mobile app** and an **Express.js/MongoDB** backend secured with JWT.

It later grew into a more production-grade parallel build aimed at real startup viability: a **Next.js + TypeScript** frontend (Radix UI, TanStack Query, Sentry, Mapbox/d3-geo for farm location mapping) backed by a **NestJS + TypeORM** service layer. That shift — from academic prototype to startup-grade architecture — even included drafting a formal Vietnamese startup proposal document.
projectItems.challenge: It started as an academic project (PRM393), but the team decided to push it into production-grade architecture aimed at real startup viability — which meant redesigning it from mobile-only into a scalable, multi-platform full stack.
highlights: Track 1 (academic): Flutter mobile app + Express.js/MongoDB backend with JWT auth
Track 2 (parallel production-grade build): Next.js + TypeScript frontend (Radix UI, TanStack Query, Sentry, Mapbox/d3-geo for farm location mapping) + NestJS + TypeORM backend
Drafted a formal Vietnamese startup proposal for the product model

projectItems.description:
An **agency platform for managing client brand content** across 5 social networks — Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, and Zalo — with content creation/approval workflows, AI Brand Voice modeling, campaign scheduling, and automated multi-platform publishing.

Architected as a **distributed 7-microservices system**: **API Gateway** (Spring Cloud Gateway, WebFlux, JWT + Redis auth & rate-limiting), **business-service** (Spring Boot 3.3.5, Java 21) handling multi-tenant logic and campaigns, **publisher-service** consuming from **RabbitMQ with Dead Letter Queue (DLQ)** exponential backoff ensuring 0% message loss, and an **AI service** (Python FastAPI, RAG & GraphRAG with ChromaDB and Neo4j) for brand voice learning and trend analysis. The frontend is a **React 18 + TypeScript + Vite** dashboard with an **Expo/React Native** companion app, fully orchestrated via **Docker Compose** on AWS EC2.
projectItems.challenge: Simultaneously publishing content across 5 social networks (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, Zalo) with 100% mission-critical reliability — requiring a 7-microservice fault-tolerant architecture (RabbitMQ DLQ exponential retry), gateway rate-limiting, and AI GraphRAG modeling brand voice.
highlights: Overall architecture of 7 distributed microservices: API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway, WebFlux, JWT+Redis), business-service (Java 21), publisher-service (RabbitMQ DLQ), AI service (FastAPI GraphRAG)
Engineered Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) exponential retry mechanism guaranteeing 0% message loss during publishing outages
Integrated RAG & GraphRAG (ChromaDB + Neo4j) to learn Brand Voice and analyze influencer/trend graph relations
React 18 + TypeScript + Vite dashboard frontend, Expo React Native mobile app, orchestrated with Docker Compose

projectItems.description:

A **Three.js / React Three Fiber** touch adds a subtle 3D flourish to the hero section, and **Framer Motion** handles page transitions. Styled with **Tailwind CSS 4** for a clean, fast-loading layout that suits tourism content well.
projectItems.challenge: Turn a dated static HTML site into a modern React experience — keeping all the rich tourism content while making sure markdown renders safely and the image-heavy pages still load fast.
highlights: Migrated from static HTML to React 19 + Vite, lazy-loading images site-wide
Safely renders markdown via DOMPurify, guarding against XSS from dynamic content
Added a subtle 3D touch to the hero using Three.js/React Three Fiber
Smooth page transitions via Framer Motion, styled with Tailwind CSS 4

React 18 + TypeScript frontend with Monaco Editor, Mermaid diagrams, Recharts dashboards, PDF export

postItems.title: Teaching a 1.5B-Parameter Model to Fix JavaScript Concurrency Bugs
postItems.excerpt: Inside ThreadLearn: fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B with QLoRA, pairing it with a BM25-based RAG pipeline, and why a small model beats GPT-3.5-turbo on a narrow domain.
postItems.content:
JavaScript runs on a single thread — a single-threaded event loop — yet handles a mountain of asynchronous tasks at once via callbacks, Promises, and async/await. That gap between "one thread" and "many overlapping tasks" creates a particularly nasty class of bug: **concurrency bugs**. According to the NodeCB study (ASE 2017), which analyzed 57 real-world bugs across 53 Node.js projects, 93% of them caused serious consequences — server crashes, data corruption, or permanent hangs. And they almost never surface when running tests in isolation.

A classic example — two requests reading then writing at the same time:

```javascript
const stock = await db.getStock(productId);   // both requests read stock = 1
await db.setStock(productId, stock - 1);       // both requests set stock = 0
// 2 units sold, but inventory only had 1 — race condition
```

Static tools like ESLint only flag the bug, they don't fix it. Calling GPT-4 costs money, requires internet, and isn't specialized for this domain. **ThreadLearn** — a WDP301 course project at FPT University I built with two teammates — took a different approach: fine-tune a small model (Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B) to specialize in exactly one class of bug, then fill the knowledge gap with RAG.

## Why a small model, not GPT-4

Three practical reasons: cost, latency, and the ability to run offline inside a firewalled enterprise environment. The team picked **Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B** — small enough to run on an 8GB GPU, yet capable since it's pretrained on hundreds of billions of code tokens — then fine-tuned it with **QLoRA** (loading the model in 4-bit NF4, training only a rank-16 LoRA adapter, roughly 0.5% of total parameters). The whole process ran on Kaggle's free 2×T4 GPUs in about 2 hours.

The fine-tuning side (783 buggy/fixed code pairs, dataset collected from GitHub plus hand-written examples) was my teammate Ha Van An's work. What I directly owned was the **RAG pipeline and API server** — the most technically substantial part, so that's what I'll detail here.

## RAG: why BM25, not vector search

With JavaScript, a developer knows exactly which API name they're looking for — `Promise.all`, `setTimeout`, `appendFile`. That's an exact-keyword-match problem, not semantic similarity. Vector search (FAISS, Chroma) needs a GPU to embed, needs a 500MB+ model, and sometimes misses exact matches because it's optimized for "roughly similar meaning" rather than "the exact keyword." **BM25** — a frequency-based search algorithm, an improvement over TF-IDF — builds an index over 2,050 documents in under 500ms, needs no GPU, and produces better results on the code domain.

The catch is BM25's default tokenizer handles code poorly: `setTimeout` gets split into `["set", "timeout"]`, `fetchAllUsers` into `["fetch", "all", "users"]`. When a query contains `setTimeout` intact, it matches more weakly against documents that got fragmented. My first version wrote a regex tokenizer to split CamelCase — it worked, but still fragmented API names when extracting keywords from input code.

The fix uses **esprima to parse code into an AST**, then only keeps tokens of type `Identifier` — function/variable names the developer chose — skipping language keywords (`async`, `await`, `for`):

```python
script = esprima.parseScript(code, options={"tolerant": True, "tokens": True})
for tok in script.tokens:
    if tok.type == "Identifier" and tok.value not in _JS_STOPWORDS:
        result.append(tok.value)
```

Direct comparison: `fs.appendFile(logPath, data)` through the regex tokenizer becomes `"fs append file path data"` — appendFile gets fragmented. Through AST extraction it becomes `"fs appendFile logPath data"` — intact. Keeping API names intact means a higher BM25 score against the right document, and the top-3 retrieved docs come back noticeably more accurate.

## Results — and why fine-tuning matters more than RAG

Evaluated on 20 hand-crafted test cases covering 8 concurrency bug categories (race conditions, event loop blocking, unhandled rejection, callback hell, zalgo, context loss, etc.), scored with Fix-Pattern Scoring (checking whether the output contains the correct fix pattern, not a hard match against a sample answer):

| Method | Pass | Partial | Fail | Pass Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-3.5-turbo zero-shot | 6 | 11 | 3 | 30% |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B (base, no fine-tune) | 8 | 9 | 3 | 40% |
| ThreadLearn RAW (fine-tuned, no RAG) | 14 | 6 | 0 | 70% |
| **ThreadLearn + RAG** | **15** | **5** | **0** | **75%** |

![Ablation chart](https://res.cloudinary.com/dvwt6npcl/image/upload/f_auto,q_auto/v1783871855/my-website/assets/blog/threadlearn/fig_ablation.png)

### Benchmark 2 — 30 real-world cases (from real npm packages on GitHub Issues)

ThreadLearn + pipeline scored **73.3% (22/30)**, beating GPT-3.5-turbo + pipeline's **65.0%** (19.5/30). Full details in `server/tests/real_world/README.md`.

### Analysis

Fine-tuning contributed **+30pp** (40% → 70%), RAG added **+5pp** (70% → 75%). 783 training samples were enough for the model to learn concrete fix patterns; RAG helps the harder cases that need context beyond the training data. No case FAILED outright — the model always produced readable code.

**3 categories still weak**: Zalgo (0/1), Double Callback (0/1), Buffer Leak (0/1) — very niche patterns, rarely represented in the dataset.

Event Loop Blocking hit **100% (5/5)** — best-covered category in the training data.

![Per-category breakdown](https://res.cloudinary.com/dvwt6npcl/image/upload/f_auto,q_auto/v1783871858/my-website/assets/blog/threadlearn/fig_category.png)

## Takeaways

A small model (~1.5B), fine-tuned on a narrow domain, **beats GPT-3.5 (175B) despite being 125x smaller** — not because it's "smarter," but because it doesn't carry irrelevant knowledge. BM25 + AST extraction is cheap, fast, and offline. When designing retrieval for code, exact keyword matching matters more than semantic similarity.

---

*Team roles: **Le Tri Trung** (AI2 — RAG Pipeline, FastAPI Server, Race Detector) · Ha Van An (AI1 — Dataset Collection, QLoRA Fine-tuning) · Nguyen Thi Thuy Hoai (Model Evaluation & Report Writing). FPT University, Da Nang.*

Code, dataset, and research paper: [github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn_AI_Trainning](https://github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn_AI_Trainning). Full PDF: `/d/FPT/threadlearn_paper-full.pdf`. Visual demo site: [github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn-AI-Visual](https://github.com/ThreadLearn/ThreadLearn-AI-Visual).
